cards.explanation: The answer is good conduct done in humility. James says to show wisdom "…by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom." Wisdom gets proven by what you do, not by what you say about yourself. A box that says "world's best cookies" still has to be opened and tasted, friends.

The answer is earthly and unspiritual. James says that kind of wisdom "…does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic." It's wisdom that never looked up, friends. It stays down here with the jealousy and the selfish ambition.

The word is disorder. James says "…where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice." Picture two people in one kitchen who both want to be head cook. Flour everywhere, and nobody is making cookies, bakers.

The one that is NOT on the list is ambitious. James's list for the wisdom from above is "…pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere." Ambitious isn't on it, friends. Selfish ambition shows up earlier, in the heart that has bitter jealousy (James 3:14).
The answer is False. James lists the wisdom from above as "impartial." It doesn't play favorites, friends. The list also includes "sincere," so there's no act and no angle.

The answer is the fruit of righteousness. James says "Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness." They sow in peace, and the fruit of righteousness is what they reap. It's the opposite of the disorder he just warned about, bakers.

The answer is True. James asks, "What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?" He points inside, friends, not at somebody else. The passions at war within are where he looks for the source.

The answer is that they ask with wrong motives. James says, "…you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures." They did ask, friends. It was the reason behind the asking that was off.

The answer is hostility toward God. James says "…friendship with the world is hostility toward God?" I think that's strong language, friends. He follows it with "…whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God."
The answer is True. Right after the hard question, James says, "But He gives us more grace." The heavy words aren't the last word, friends. Grace comes next.

The answer is the humble. The Scripture says, "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble." James is pulling that from Proverbs 3:34. Same line, two kinds of people, and the humble get the grace, bakers.

The answer is that the devil will flee from them. James says, "Resist the devil, and he will flee from you." It comes right after "Submit yourselves, then, to God." So the resisting happens alongside submitting to God, friends.
The answer is True. James says, "Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you." That's a promise, friends, and it comes with an invitation. You take a step and He draws near.

The answer is False. James says, "Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom." It's a hard word, and it comes right after he tells them to cleanse their hands and purify their hearts. I'm a stamper who loves a good laugh, friends, but I take this one soberly.

The word is exalt. James says, "Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you." Humbling comes first, and the lifting up is His part. It matches the grace for the humble back in verse 6, bakers.

The answer is a judge of it. James says, "…if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it." You were supposed to be doing the law, friends. Instead you've moved over to the judge's chair.

The answer is the One able to save and destroy. James says, "There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy." He alone holds both the law and the verdict, friends. That's why he follows it with "But who are you to judge your neighbor?"
